issues.description: The problem statement and UML require messageOnMilk() to return a String (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning boolean and the Seal and Goat implementations print the message and return true. This contradicts the specified return type and expected behavior and will confuse students about what to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable interface and implementations with the problem specification: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String, and have Seal and Goat return the formatted string (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked") instead of printing and returning boolean. Alternatively, if boolean was intended, update the problem statement/UML to state a boolean return and adjust examples accordingly.

issues.description: The method messageOnMilk() is expected by the problem statement and the template Main usage to return a String containing the text "[Animal Type] [name] is milked", but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a boolean and implementations print the message instead of returning it. This mismatch between the expected return type (String) and the solution's return type (boolean) creates confusion for students mapping the requirement to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String and have implementations return the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (do not print inside the method). Update implementations (Seal, Goat) to return the String and let callers (e.g., Main or Farm) print it. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to expect a boolean, but preferred fix is to match the problem's String-returning contract.
